- File sits under fixtures/app3y/ but is a 3Z. Directory name is not evidence of form type.

- Part 2 holdings, (A)/(B) enumerated in BOTH columns and must be matched pairwise: "(A) 3,326,667 shares", "(B) 500,000 shares". Class is written only as "shares" — the strings "ordinary" and "fully paid ordinary" appear nowhere in the document.
- qty_before/qty_after correctly left empty. A 3Z has no before/after structure, and the (A)+(B) sum of 3,826,667 must NOT be back-filled into qty_after: it is not attributable to the ordinary class without inference, and a substantive default here would be wrong.
- The (A)/(B) markers are holder enumeration, not transaction enumeration. A parser counting them as transactions wrongly reports 2.
- Malformed Part 2 (A): "Sunshine Group Investments Pty Ltd <Sunshine Group Inv Fam A/C – Director" — angle bracket opened, never closed. (B) "James Dack Real Estate Pty Ltd <James Dack Super Fund A/C>" closes correctly. A greedy <...> regex will swallow from (A) into (B). (B) also wraps mid-name with justified multi-space runs ("James  Dack  Real  Estate  Pty"), so whitespace must be collapsed.
- Part 3: all four cells read "N A" — space, not "N/A" or "NA". A "N/A"/"Nil" matcher treats these as populated.
- Two pages; no covering letter, no signature block, no date-signed/lodgement field.

CORRECTED: three points in the first reading.
1. The first reading attributes "– Director" as "the nature of interest" for Part 2 without qualification. It belongs to holder (A) ONLY; holder (B) carries no nature-of-interest text at all. A pairwise parser must not carry "Director" across to (B) — (B)'s nature of interest is unstated and should be recorded as unknown, not inherited from (A).
2. "Rule 3.19A.3" is listed in the first reading among "boilerplate dates that can be mis-captured". It is a listing-rule reference, not a date. The genuine boilerplate dates are "Introduced 30/9/2001." and the version stamp "11/3/2002". The first reading's assessment of "11/3/2002" is otherwise right — it appears in the page-1 footer ("11/3/2002  Appendix 3Z Page 1") and again in the page-2 footer ("Appendix 3Z Page 2  11/3/2002"), i.e. twice, in footers, not in headers.
3. "post-dates the Date of last notice ... by ~10 months" — the actual gap from 27 October 2025 to 18 August 2026 is 9 months 22 days. Trivial, but the framing matters: a ceased-date later than the last notice is the normal ordering on a 3Z, not an anomaly to flag. (Reading run date 2026-08-19, so cessation was the prior day.)

direct_or_indirect deliberately left empty: a 3Z has no direct/indirect field. The split is inferable from structure (Part 1 direct = Nil; Part 2 indirect = 3,826,667 across two holders) but must not be synthesized into a transaction-level field when no transaction is described.

documents.notes: Appendix 3Z (Final Director's Interest Notice), Rule 3.19A.3, 2 pages, no covering letter. Being a 3Z it has no change/acquisition/disposal/consideration/closed-period fields at all — those are absent by form design, not blank; transaction_count is therefore 0 and closed_period 'na'. There is no "Date of change"; instead "Date that director ceased to be director | 19 August 2026" (verbatim), which is the sole event date on the form. ABN printed with spaces: "37 142 925 684"; no ACN given. Verified all figures against the document; the ABN also passes the ATO modulus-89 checksum (weighted sum 534, 534 mod 89 = 0), confirming no digit transposition in transcription. Part 1 lists TWO classes in one cell as a lettered list: a) 8,991,870 Fully Paid Ordinary Shares; b) 1,621,622 Unlisted Options Ex $0.04, expiring 27 June 2028 — the "$0.04" is an option exercise price and must not be read as consideration. A SECOND ordinary-shares figure appears in Part 2: "65,120,000 Fully Paid Ordinary Shares" held indirectly via Dalraida Holdings Pty Ltd; a greedy regex for "Fully Paid Ordinary Shares" will match this too or sum the two. Part 3 is headed "Part 3 – Director's interests in contracts – N/A" with all four cells literally "N/A". Date-regex traps: the template footers "Introduced 30/9/2001." and "11/3/2002" (the latter on both pages) are form template dates, not event dates. CORRECTED: the first reading called the chronology "odd" because date of last notice (4 July 2025) precedes cessation (19 August 2026). That is not an anomaly — it is the required and expected ordering on every 3Z, since the last notice necessarily predates the director leaving the board. Flagging it as odd would make a validator raise a false alarm on essentially every 3Z in the corpus; the correct anomaly rule is the reverse test (last notice AFTER cessation). Note also that cessation 19 August 2026 is the current date, so event_date and knowable_at coincide here. CORRECTED: the first reading listed only "30/9/2001" and "11/3/2002" as date-regex traps but missed a third and more dangerous one — "expiring 27 June 2028" inside Part 1 item b). That is an option expiry date sitting in the securities cell, closer to the extraction target than either footer, and a date-picker scanning the Part 1 block will grab it. CORRECTED (scope flag, not a transcription error): qty_after = 8,991,870 is correctly transcribed but is the DIRECT registered holding only. The director's total ordinary-share relevant interest at cessation is 74,111,870 (8,991,870 direct + 65,120,000 indirect) — the indirect parcel is 7.2x the direct one, so any consumer reading qty_after as "total ordinary shares held at cessation" understates it by 65,120,000. Strictly, a 3Z states no post-transaction balance at all (qty_before/qty_after are 3Y change-notice fields); 8,991,870 is retained as the closest analogue — the final registered direct balance — and must carry a direct-only coverage flag downstream rather than being fed into a total-holdings replay. Additional parser trap not previously noted: the file is stored under fixtures/app3y/ but is an Appendix 3Z — directory path is not a reliable form-type signal; classify from the document header only.

Checked against the PDF and against the pypdf text layer page by page. CORRECTED (one factual error in the first reading's notes): the document-control string "3461-0342-1486, v. 1" appears ONLY on PDF pages 2 and 3. It does NOT appear on the second form's pages. Verified by grep over the full text layer: hits at page 2 and page 3 only; pages 1, 4, 5, 6 have no occurrence. The first reading's parenthetical "(and again on the second form's pages)" is wrong. Practical consequence: the string is present on exactly 2 of 6 pages and is a usable (though not authoritative) marker of the FIRST form's continuation pages, not a document-wide footer.

Everything else in the first reading's notes is confirmed, plus these additional traps found on re-read:

SPLITTING / PAGINATION (the first reading understated this):
- PDF page 1 has NO page footer at all - there is no "Appendix 3Y Page 1" on it. The reset marker "01/01/2011 Appendix 3Y Page 1" appears only on PDF page 4, and in reading order it is extracted ABOVE the "Rule 3.19A.2" header of the second form, i.e. the footer-shaped reset marker and the start of the new form sit on the same page. A splitter that cuts on the footer will put the boundary in the wrong place, and one that looks for a matching "Page 1" footer on the first form will not find one.
- Footer field order is not stable: pages 2, 3 and 6 read "01/01/2011 Appendix 3Y Page N", but page 5 reads "Appendix 3Y Page 2 01/01/2011" (date last). A regex anchored on date-first will silently miss page 5.
- The two forms use different footer templates entirely (first form: footer + doc-control line; second form: footer only).

TRANSACTION A IS A CONVERSION, SO THE FORM UNDER-REPORTS DISPOSALS:
- Transaction A both acquires 125,000 ordinary shares and extinguishes 125,000 performance rights, but "Number disposed" records only B's 53,571. The Class cell likewise lists one class per lettered transaction (A = ordinary, B = 2027 rights), never the rights leg of A. A parser that treats "number disposed" as the total securities disposed will understate the 2027 rights movement by 125,000, and only the disappearance of the 178,571 line from the "after" block reveals it. Do not infer the missing leg silently - it is an unstated fact.
- Transaction B is a lapse recorded under "Number disposed": a disposal with no counterparty and no consideration.
